title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 5 Lesson 1: Smooth Inclined Planes custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 50\text{ N}$), calculate the component of weight acting down the plane and the component of weight acting perpendicular to the plane.

A particle of mass $6\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium on a smooth slope inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal by a force of magnitude $P$ acting up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate $P$ and the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the slope on the particle.

A particle of mass $4\text{ kg}$ is kept in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal by a horizontal force of magnitude $P$ directed towards the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate $P$.
For the particle in Drill 3 ($m = 4\text{ kg}$, slope angle $45^\circ$, horizontal holding force $P = 40\text{ N}$), calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane on the particle.

A box of mass $10\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal by a rope pulling at an angle of $20^\circ$ above the slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the rope correct to 3 significant figures.

A particle $A$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline and supports a vertically hanging particle $B$ of mass $m_B$. The system is in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate $m_B$.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m = 13\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{5}{12}$ (so $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$). A force of magnitude $P$ acts up the line of greatest slope, holding the block in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 130\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving parallel to the line of greatest slope, calculate the holding force $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving perpendicular to the plane, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane, and state the total contact force exerted by the plane on the block.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 8\text{ kg}$ ($W = 80\text{ N}$) is held in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal by a horizontal force of magnitude $P$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving parallel to the inclined plane, show that $P = \frac{80\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 46.2\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane on the particle.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m = 8\text{ kg}$ is kept in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal by an applied force of magnitude $100\text{ N}$ directed at an angle $\theta$ below the line of greatest slope ($0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$), pressing into the incline. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 80\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel to the inclined plane, calculate the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane on the block correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $m_A = 5\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ runs up the line of greatest slope, passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the top of the incline, and supports a vertically hanging block $B$ of mass $m_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W_A = 50\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the system is held in equilibrium by the suspended mass $B$, find the tension $T$ in the string and determine the value of $m_B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If instead block $B$ has mass $4\text{ kg}$, calculate the extra force $F$ that must be applied to block $A$ directed down the slope to keep the system in equilibrium, and find the magnitude of the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley.

questions.prompt: A fixed smooth wedge has two triangular faces inclined at $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ to the horizontal. A particle $A$ of mass $m_A = 6\text{ kg}$ on the $30^\circ$ face is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the apex to a particle $B$ of mass $m_B$ resting on the $60^\circ$ face. The system is in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving parallel to the $30^\circ$ face, calculate the tension $T$ in the string.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving parallel to the $60^\circ$ face, calculate the mass $m_B$ of particle $B$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reactions $R_A$ and $R_B$ exerted by the two faces on particles $A$ and $B$ respectively.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $M = 12\text{ kg}$ ($W = 120\text{ N}$) is held on a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the crate is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force of magnitude $P$, calculate $P$ and the normal reaction $R_1$ exerted by the plane.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If instead the crate is held in equilibrium by a force $Q$ inclined at an angle $\beta$ to the line of greatest slope ($-\frac{\pi}{2} < \beta < \frac{\pi}{2}$), show that the minimum magnitude of $Q$ occurs when $\beta = 0$, and find this minimum force $Q_{\min}$ and the corresponding normal reaction $R_2$.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 50\text{ N}$) rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). Two external forces act on the particle: a constant horizontal force $F_1 = 20\text{ N}$ pushing directly into the incline, and a light string pulling with tension $T$ at an angle $\theta$ above the line of greatest slope ($0^\circ \leqslant \theta < 90^\circ$). The particle is in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel to the line of greatest slope, show that $T\cos\theta = 14\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane in terms of $T$ and $\theta$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the critical angle $\theta_c$ at which the particle is on the point of losing contact with the plane ($R = 0$), and calculate the corresponding string tension $T$.
